behavior: Forages in trees, shrubs, low vegetation, and sometimes on the ground, eating mainly seeds and buds along with fruit and insects. Often feeds in small flocks outside the nesting season; flight is undulating. Courting males hop with drooped wings and a raised tail, sing softly, and may make a short fluttering ascent.
field_marks: Stocky, large-headed finch with a short, distinctly notched tail
Adult male washed raspberry-red across the head, breast, and back
Male has brown wings and a cloudy whitish lower belly, and typically lacks obvious dark stripes on the sides
Female and immature are brown with coarse streaking below, a pale eyebrow, and a dark cheek or throat-side line
Dark eye and dusky pink-brown legs and feet
habitat: Breeds mainly in cool coniferous forest and mixed woodland, including forest edges and wooded stream corridors. Outside the breeding season it also uses shrublands, old fields, hedgerows, semi-open woods, and planted areas with trees.
